endorsements.quote: The most promising solution lies in developing highly specialized “expert AIs” trained not on the chaotic internet, but on meticulously curated, gold standard datasets.

unlisted_practices: Obtain explicit written consent from body donors before using their bodies in AI training.
Obtain explicit written consent for the use of medical images from hospital datasets, such as CT and MRI scans, in AI training.
Protect existing published medical illustrations from unauthorized use for AI training or compensate their authors or copyright holders.
Use reinforcement learning from human feedback, with expert illustrators and surgeons continuously rating outputs, to train models to prioritize accuracy.
Integrate generative AI with a rule-based 3D anatomy atlas so the software generates the accurate 3D structure and the AI is limited to applying styles, angles, and lighting.
Fine-tune existing powerful generative models on specialized, curated anatomical data to steer them toward anatomical precision.
Do not use AI-generated anatomical illustrations as a replacement for cadaver dissection and prosection-based education.

screen.reason: This paper is a critical commentary and viewpoint calling for functionally aware AI and human supervision in generative anatomical illustration, discussing limitations and future directions rather than presenting original empirical data.
